How to spot a fake

  • Check the stitching and the wash-care label
  • Compare hardware, like Chrome Hearts silver, against verified photos
  • Verify the seller’s history and listing details
  • Match the piece to its season and production run

Design notes

Milestone 3 write-up. This section is not part of the homepage design.

Menu (7 pages)

Home, Deep Dives, Authentication, Price Watch, Primers, Collectors, Newsletter

Top 5 designs I liked from competitors and how I used them

  1. Introspective Magazine, large editorial hero. I liked the big photo with a strong headline, so my homepage opens with a large runway photo carousel and a headline.
  2. Introspective Magazine, white space. I liked how the spacing makes the site feel high-end, so I kept wide gaps between sections and used a white background.
  3. Clair by Rebag, clear price display. I liked how it shows value at a glance, so I made a Price Watch box with prices and up or down changes.
  4. Clair by Rebag, open and trustworthy information. I liked how it builds trust by showing its reasoning, so I added a “How to spot a fake” checklist.
  5. Archive-fashion Instagram accounts, photo grids. I liked the tight grid of outfit photos, so I made a “Labels we cover” grid with a photo for each of the 12 brands.

Design principles

  • Contrast: red buttons and links on a white background, and large serif headlines over small body text.
  • Alignment: a 992px centered wrapper and a consistent grid (3 columns for cards, 4 for brands).
  • Repetition: the same card style, the same two fonts, and the same red throughout.
  • Proximity: each photo is grouped with its title and description, with bigger gaps between sections.
